clinician.final_diagnosis: Small bowel obstruction caused by endometriosis of the right round ligament
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 37-year-old woman with a remote history of endometriosis (treated with two prior laparoscopic ablations) and prior cholecystectomy presented to the emergency room with one day of upper abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Physical examination revealed non-distended abdomen with epigastric and right upper/lower quadrant tenderness. Abdominal series demonstrated a prominent small bowel loop in the right lower quadrant with air-fluid levels. CT imaging confirmed partial small bowel obstruction with a transition point at the terminal ileum and an adjacent 1 cm soft-tissue nodule. Three days after admission, the patient underwent diagnostic laparoscopy, which identified a 2 cm lesion in the ileum located 4.8 cm from the ileocecal valve with scattered adhesions involving the terminal ileum and right colon. A right hemicolectomy was performed. Pathology confirmed endometriosis involving the muscularis propria and serosa of the terminal ileum, ascending colon, and appendix, with a 1.8 × 1.5 × 1.1 cm endometrial mass identified as the cause of the small bowel obstruction. The diagnosis of endometriosis of the right round ligament is supported by the patient's known history of endometriosis, the anatomic location of the obstructing lesion in proximity to the right lower quadrant, and the pathologic confirmation of endometrial tissue in the resected specimen.
